processing: A regional brand rather than one recipe; production from growing through packing must take place inside the registered area. Most of what it covers is made by the usual green tea steps of fixing, rolling and drying.
harvest_season: Dates vary by county and are little documented for the brand as a whole. As with other Qinba mountain greens, spring tea is the prized picking.
appearance_dry: Varies by maker and style; typically fine green strands.
appearance_wet: Tender green leaf, varying with the grade.
taste_profile: Clear, long aroma with a fresh, mellow taste and a sweet return.

brewing.notes: Styles differ under the brand, so begin as for any Chinese green and adjust. Finer, downy leaf wants slightly cooler water.

vintage_note: Sold as a current-year green, usually by spring harvest, as is usual for its class. As this is a regional brand covering many makers, the maker and the harvest date tell you more than the name does.
description:
Ankang Selenium Tea is a regional public brand for green tea from Ankang, in southeast Shaanxi. The one thing that sets it apart is the soil: the area is promoted as China's largest natural selenium-rich zone, and the name is built around that.

It is a geographical indication covering 82 towns across nine counties and districts, including Ziyang, Pingli and Hanyin. So it is not one tea with one look, and individual teas from the area may have their own names too. The rule is that growing, picking and processing all stay inside that zone.

The general description is a tender green liquor, a clear lasting aroma, and a fresh, mellow taste with a sweet finish. Treat it like other mountain greens: water a little off the boil and short steeps at first.

When buying, go by maker and harvest. The selenium is a marketing focus and health claims around it deserve caution. What you can judge in the cup is freshness.
history:
Promotional accounts trace Ankang tea back some 3,000 years to the Western Zhou, which is a regional claim rather than a documented line for this tea. Firmer ground is Lu Yu's Tang-era Classic of Tea, which records tea from the valleys of Jinzhou, the old name for this area.

The brand itself is modern. The certification trademark passed review in 2018, and the brand was then listed among China's regional agricultural public brands for 2019. It sits alongside Hanzhong Xianhao and Jingyang Fu tea as one of the leading Shaanxi tea names.
